label: The CLI vitest step is 776-950s (65 percent of the 1215s check job) because both vitest projects set fileParallelism:false, serialising 183 CLI test files; neither setting carries a comment explaining why, and the risk that serialisation is load-bearing for shared fixtures must be tested before flipping it

spec-kit-check.yml sets no timeout-minutes on any of its three jobs, so a hung serial vitest or bash lane runs to the GitHub default instead of the ~20 minutes a healthy run takes; only 6 of 33 workflow files set any timeout at all, and the two longest jobs in the repo (strict-pass-freshness-report 2568s and deep-loop-runtime 688s) are among the unguarded set or barely guarded

No workflow in the repo passes cache:npm to actions/setup-node (zero cache: hits across 33 files), so every job pays a cold install: 46-52s in the check job's three npm ci calls, 37-42s re-installing five package trees plus pyyaml in the doctor-scripts job, and 8-14s re-installing the workspace in the mirrors job, i.e. three cold installs of overlapping dependency sets per single run

actions/checkout costs 48-52s per job in every sampled workflow and 10362s across 207 of 230 sampled jobs, which is 25.6 percent of all sampled runner-seconds at a mean of 50.1s per job; small workflows are almost entirely clone: command-tree-parity's Hermes job is 74s wall of which 50s is checkout and 1s is the actual comparison, and No new broken citations is 79s wall of which 73s is checkout

Only 1 of 33 workflows declares a concurrency group and that one sets cancel-in-progress:false by design because a cancelled trigger-index rebuild would leave the index stale; with 40 pushes to main in 23.5h and a 20-minute check job, superseded spec-kit-check runs are therefore billed in full

The two cheap jobs in spec-kit-check are almost pure setup: the mirrors job spends 50s on checkout plus 8-14s installing the workspace to run nine --check scripts that take 0-1s, and the doctor-scripts job spends 50s on checkout plus 37-42s installing five dependency trees to run 55-67s of suites; the sk-vision step additionally downloads bun and runs a full frozen-lockfile install to produce one bundle file

The spec-kit-check paths list includes the generated mirror trees .codex, .claude, .cursor, .devin and .pi for both push and pull_request, so a commit touching only mirror output re-runs the 791s CLI suite, 164s legacy lanes and 132s runtime suite even though none of those read the mirror trees, when the 62s mirrors job is the only thing that needs them

Splitting the check job into four parallel jobs lowers wall-clock from 1215s to ~891s but raises billed minutes from 26 to 32 per run because each split job re-pays a 50s clone, a 47s install and its own ceil-to-minute rounding, whereas fixing fileParallelism alone takes the same single job to ~690s wall at ~17 billed minutes; sharding the CLI vitest project is a cost-neutral fallback at roughly 20 billed minutes for a 3x wall win

Billed runner minutes are charged per job as ceil(job seconds / 60), so splitting one job into N parallel jobs multiplies per-job overhead and rounding: wall-clock and billed cost move in opposite directions unless the longest job itself gets shorter

A vitest project with fileParallelism:false has a runtime equal to the sum of all its test files rather than the longest one, so its cost grows linearly with file count and cannot be improved by making individual files faster

direction: Shard the CLI vitest project as the primary speed fix for spec-kit-check
reason: Sharding and job-splitting both re-pay the 50s clone, the 47s install and per-job minute rounding; measured arithmetic puts a 4-way shard at ~20 billed minutes versus today's 21 for the whole check job, so sharding is a wall-clock tool at best cost-neutral, and the root cause (fileParallelism:false) is cheaper to fix and also helps the runtime project and deep-loop-runtime's 688s job

direction: Treat the small workflows' 60-100s wall times as test cost to optimise
reason: Step data shows 69-79s jobs are 50s checkout plus 1s of real work, so there is nothing to optimise inside those jobs; the only levers are fewer jobs and cancelling superseded runs
